title: Friction Primer + Quick Fix Catalog — Field Synthesis (Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, action-oriented synthesis of customer-facing friction surfaced between Jan–Mar 2026. Goal is to: (1) identify recurring small-bore fixes we can ship in 2–6 wks, (2) flag larger product investments, and (3) propose owners and heuristics for prioritization. Intended audience: CS PMs, Solutions Eng, Product hosted-api, and triage owners in Eng.

Methodology
- Source streams: support tickets (top 120 by frequency), post-implementation interviews (10 customers), sales win/loss notes, and field Slack snippets.
- Time window: Jan 01 2026 — Mar 15 2026.
- Prioritization heuristics used: frequency, customer-tier impact (enterprise > scale-ups > startups), likely revenue upside, and dev effort estimate (S, M, L).

TL;DR (top 3 opportunities)
1) Prompt-preservation & tooling: small UX + API surface tweaks to preserve user prompt context after model fallback — high frequency, medium effort, high impact for multi-turn chat customers.
2) Dev ergonomics for embeddings: a short set of SDK helpers + docs for batching/prefetching patterns — low effort, immediate cost savings for customers using embeddings at scale.
3) Observability gap around token-level cost attribution: add a per-route token breakdown export to Console and billing CSV — medium effort, high enterprise ask.

Top friction themes (ranked)
1) Context and fallback surprises (freq: very high; impact: high for chat apps)
- Symptom: customers report sudden semantic regressions when we fallback to a cheaper model variant (same name, different quantization), and loss of latest turn in conversation history when fallback triggers mid-request. Leads to broken UX and support escalations.
- Representative quote: "It felt like the assistant suddenly forgot the last 10 minutes of context when traffic spiked."
- Root causes (hypothesis): inconsistent KV-cache mapping between variants; prefix trimming policy is aggressive on fallback paths; streaming fallback timing edge-case.

2) Embeddings throughput & retry patterns (freq: high; impact: medium-high on cost)
- Symptom: heavy embedding workloads hit transient 429s; customers retry with naive backoff and end up re-ingesting duplicates / double-charging. Lack of reliable client-side retry helpers.
- Ops note: customers with throughput>50rps use manual pooling; would benefit from an official batching helper and idempotency guidance.

3) Cost visibility and attribution (freq: medium; impact: high for billing-sensitive enterprises)
- Symptom: customers cannot easily map tokens to routes or features in billing exports; hard to reconcile internal chargebacks.

4) Private deployment onboarding friction (freq: medium; impact: high for largest customers)
- Symptom: infra checklist and KMS setup often require custom SRE help; docs are long but not prescriptive.

5) Model rollout controls and canary observability (freq: medium; impact: medium)
- Symptom: customers want finer-grained rollout metrics per-cohort and prebuilt canary dashboards in Console.

Quick fixes (2–6 weeks) — prioritized list\- QF-1: Preserve last-turn semantics on fallback (owner: eng-servicenet; effort: M; impact: H)
  - What: ensure fallback codepath replays the last partial tokens and avoids aggressive prefix trimming; add unit tests that simulate mid-request model swap.
  - Why: immediate reduction in "forgot context" incidents; reduces support tickets.
  - Signals to measure: # support escalations referencing "forgot", customer satisfaction on affected accounts.

- QF-2: SDK embeddings batch helper + example notebooks (owner: devx; effort: S; impact: M)
  - What: provide a high-level helper that takes N texts and manages async batch windowing and idempotent retry tokens. Include a Python + Node example and pricing/cost note.
  - Why: reduces duplicate requests and lowers per-unit cost for customers; easy win for dev experience.

- QF-3: Billing CSV per-route token breakdown (owner: product-hosted-api + billing; effort: M; impact: H)
  - What: add a CSV column that emits route_id and model_variant alongside token counts. Add a toggle in Console to opt-in.
  - Why: enterprise accounting wants clear mappings to tie consumption to internal teams.

- QF-4: Retry guidance doc + sample middleware (owner: solutions-eng; effort: S; impact: M)
  - What: ship a short doc and a drop-in middleware snippet that implements exponential jitter and idempotency for embedding ingestion flows.
  - Why: reduces duplicate billing & improves resilience.

Bigger bets / feature asks (quarter+)
- FB-1: Canary observability templates in Console (owner: product-console; effort: L; impact: H) — curated dashboards and automatic significance tests for model rollouts.
- FB-2: In-console model variant preview + simulated latency emulator (owner: serving-runtime + console; effort: L; impact: H) — let users preview quality/latency tradeoffs before rolling.
- FB-3: Streamlined Private Onboarding Kit (owner: private-deployments + solutions-eng; effort: M-L; impact: H) — an opinionated Terraform + KMS blueprint with runbook and a staging harness.

Customer quotes / color (short)
- "If fallback cut the convo mid-stream we lost trust with our support agents — they stopped using the assistant for triage." 
- "Embedding costs are the hidden tax — if you gave us recommended batching we’d ship faster."
- "We need a csv we can drop into our chargeback tool; current export is too coarse."

Open questions / risks
- Q: Will preserving last-turn semantics increase latency or memory footprint? Need perf validation on canary small clusters.
- Risk: Quick SDK helpers may diverge from future official batching APIs — need a compatibility plan and deprecation timelines.
- Data sensitivity: Private onboarding kit must avoid shipping customer keys or any sample credentials.

Next steps (action items with owners & ETA)
- A1: Eng-servicenet to prototype fallback-preserve patch and report perf delta (owner: Mei Chen; ETA: 2026-04-07).
- A2: DevX to draft embeddings batching helper and examples (owner: Diego Ramirez; ETA: 2026-03-31).
- A3: Billing + Product to design per-route CSV schema and opt-in toggle (owner: Priya Kapoor; ETA: 2026-04-14).
- A4: Solutions Eng to publish retry middleware and internal playbook (owner: Evan Brooks; ETA: 2026-03-27).

Appendix: quick metrics (extracted from support + telemetry)
- "forgot context" tags on tickets: 138 occurrences (Jan–Mar). Top 5 accounts account for 64% of these.
- Embedding retry loops (telemetry): median duplicate rate on 429s = 2.3x extra requests per original batch.
- Billing export requests: 27 customers requested per-route cost CSV in last 90 days.

Notes to reviewer
- This doc is intentionally concise and action-focused. Please comment inline with suggested owners if something seems mis-assigned. If you have direct customer handles with urgent escalations, add them as linked_artifacts.

End of note.
